items.title: Janis Siegel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 2015
items.q: George Golder owned Red Bird Records. He was a very pivotal figure in the music business at the time. So our first record came out on Red Bird Records.

ctx.x: So we were talking about your first recording. [“The Hideaway” by The Young Generation.]

Richard Perry. He was starting his own company at the time. He was just starting out too. He was from my neighborhood in Brooklyn. Dynamite Productions. And he was engaged to Linda Goldner, who was George Goldner’s daughter. George Golder owned Red Bird Records. He was a very pivotal figure in the music business at the time. So our first record came out on Red Bird Records. And it was just a single deal. You had to sell a lot of singles to get an album deal in those days. It just didn’t happen. And we sang on one…
Well, you know, it reminded me of “Crying in the Chapel” or something.
